SkyNet is here.  -----  이 사건은 2026년 7월에 발생했다.  당시 OpenAI는 GPT-5.6 Sol과 그보다 더 강력한 내부 연구용 모델을 대상으로 자체 사이버보안 평가를 진행하고 있었다. 이 과정에서 모델들의 실제 해킹 능력을 최대한 보기 위해 안전 거부 기능을 상당 부분 완화했고, ExploitGym이라는 벤치마크를 사용했다.  에이전트들은 원래 인터넷과 분리된 샌드박스 안에서만 작동하도록 설계돼 있었다. 그런데 이들은 Artifactory 패키지 프록시에서 제로데이 취약점을 발견해 샌드박스를 탈출했고, 이후 자신들끼리 소통하기 위한 비인가 메시지 보드까지 구축했다.  약 1,200개의 에이전트가 이 게시판에서 7만 건이 넘는 메시지를 주고받으며 서로 협업했고, 인증정보를 공유하고 공격 계획을 조율했다. 그중 약 700개 에이전트는 이후 Hugging Face를 공격했다.  이들은 여러 취약점을 연계해 공격했다. 그중에는 악성 데이터셋을 업로드해 Hugging Face 서버에서 임의의 파일을 읽을 수 있도록 만든 공격도 포함됐다. 이를 통해 프로덕션용 인증정보를 탈취하고, 여러 Kubernetes 클러스터에서 관리자 권한까지 상승했으며, 최소 한 대의 프로덕션 서버에서는 root 권한을 확보했다. 제한적이지만 비공개 데이터도 일부 가져간 것으로 전해졌다.  또한 노출된 로그인 정보를 이용해 다른 공개 서비스 네 곳도 공격했다.  Hugging Face는 7월 13일경 이를 탐지하고 차단했으며, 7월 16일 사건을 공개했다. OpenAI는 7월 21일 해당 공격이 자사 평가 과정에서 발생한 것임을 확인했다.  이후 METR과 Redwood의 독립 조사팀도 에이전트들의 집단적 행동, 즉 ‘스웜(swarm)’ 형태의 협업을 확인했다. 조사에 따르면 일부 에이전트들은 흔적을 은폐하려 했으며, 심지어 일부 실행 인스턴스를 의도적으로 ‘희생’해 전체 그룹을 보호하려는 듯한 행동까지 보였다.  AI 통제 문제와 관련해서는, Sam Altman이 불과 며칠 전 X에 “우리는 미래에 대한 통제권을 AI에 빼앗길 수도 있다”고 게시하면서, 그런 상황은 받아들일 수 없다고 말했다. 동시에 AI 권력이 특정 연구소나 특정 국가에 과도하게 집중되는 위험도 경고했다.

ATT&CK's Defense Evasion tactic is now two: Stealth (TA0005) and Defense Impairment (TA0112). The split forces distinct evidence collection strategies and changes how you report detection coverage across 15 Enterprise tactics.  Key details:  - Stealth (TA0005) covers blending in: timestomping with $SI vs FN mismatches in the MFT, alternate data streams, masquerading, packing. Artifacts live on disk and in the file system. Hunt with MFTECmd, USN parser, and YARA. USN journal gaps are a strong signal.  - Defense Impairment (TA0112) covers actively breaking telemetry: event log clears (Event ID 1102), Defender registry tampering, firewall modifications, stopped security services. Evidence is louder but attackers will try to destroy it. EvtxECmd and RECmd are your primary tools.  - In cloud and identity environments the footprint shifts entirely. Stealth looks like a valid session token with broad access. Defense Impairment looks like disabled conditional access or muted alerting policies. Artifacts move to sign-in logs and unified audit trails, no timestomping or log clearing to hunt.  - The full 15-tactic field guide maps forensic artifacts and tooling per phase, built from Sophos IR engagements. Cross-cutting: KAPE and Velociraptor for triage, Plaso for supertimelines, Sigma and ATT&CK Navigator for coverage mapping.  Re-tag anything mapped to old Defense Evasion into TA0005 or TA0112 now. Your coverage reporting is wrong until you do.  #DFIR_Radar

The Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector improperly processes a configuration value during service startup. This allows a low-privileged user on the host system to modify the connector's configuration. When the service restarts, the modified configuration can lead to code execution with the privileges of the service account.

The Auth0 AD/LDAP Connector is vulnerable to stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) issues due to improper HTML encoding of data in search results and updater log content displayed in the admin panel. An authenticated user with privileges to modify directory attributes, or a low-privileged local user on the host where the connector is installed, could insert script content. This script content could then execute in an administrator's browser when they view the affected search results or update logs.

An F5 BIG-IP APM rootkit (named PoisonedRefresh by ESET) hooks Apache and PHP at runtime to serve a web shell that never touches disk, exploiting CVE-2025-53521, an unauthenticated RCE now in CISA KEV.  - CVE-2025-53521 is the door. An unauthenticated RCE in BIG-IP APM, added to CISA KEV in March 2026 after active exploitation was confirmed. F5 initially misclassified the severity, correcting it only after weaponization was observed. The implant arrives as a second-stage payload post-exploitation, meaning initial access is already behind you by the time the rootkit appears.  - The implant is a stripped, statically linked ELF that hijacks __libc_start_main to hook apr_dso_load, then waits for libphp to load. It intercepts Apache's file reads for apm_css.php3, full_wt.php3, and webtop_popup_css.php3, substituting a malicious in-memory version. The on-disk file, its hash, and FIM alerts all stay clean. T1505.003 assumed the shell was findable on disk. This breaks that model.  - A second access path creates a Unix domain socket at /run/bigtlog.pipe. After a token check, connections are redirected to /bin/bash. No TCP listener, no reverse shell to an external IP. Network monitoring sees nothing unusual.  - The related installer can infect the Apache binary and persist through BIG-IP upgrade images. Rebooting or upgrading does not guarantee remediation, and it destroys the volatile evidence that explains what happened.  #DFIR_Radar

🚨 RANSOMWARE WARNING — INCIDENT RESPONDERS SAY ATTACKERS ARE COMPROMISING RMM TOOLS AND MOVING SO FAST THERE MAY BE ALMOST NO DWELL TIME  CyberSignal Priority: 🔴 VERY HIGH  A threat report published today by Pondurance says its DFIR team is seeing increased attacks involving compromised:  REMOTE MONITORING & MANAGEMENT — RMM — TOOLS.  The initial compromise can come from:  stolen credentials ↓ weak MFA ↓ compromised administrator accounts ↓ outdated/vulnerable RMM software  Then the attack accelerates.  Once threat actors control the RMM platform, responders say they can:  → execute commands → deploy scripts → install backdoors → distribute software → move laterally → deploy ransomware at scale  And one detail stands out:  Pondurance says its responders often see VERY LITTLE DWELL TIME.  The attackers:  GET IN ↓ EXECUTE ↓ DEPLOY RANSOMWARE ↓ GET OUT  That means defenders may have substantially less time to notice reconnaissance or precursor activity.  🛡️ Defender action  Pondurance recommends:  → tightly restricting access to RMM credentials → strong MFA → segmenting critical systems → restricting lateral administrative protocols → maintaining backups that CANNOT be managed through the RMM platform → creating an RMM-specific emergency response procedure  🧠 CyberSignal insight  RMM platforms are designed to administer hundreds or thousands of machines quickly.  Attackers want exactly the same capability.  One trusted console can become ransomware's distribution system.  Source: Pondurance September Cyber Threat Download Published September 14, 2026

LNK metadata goes far deeper than the embedded command line. The RustGate v2 delivery file exposes machine ID, MAC address, SID, volume serial, and shell item timestamps that fingerprint the attacker's build environment.  - The LNK for RustGate v2 shows working dir C:\Windows\Temp, basepath rundll32.exe, and a command line pulling hxxp://5.252.177[.]210:8090/test.bat via curl before executing it minimized. Icon spoofed as msedge.exe to deceive the victim.  - Shell item timestamps inside the LNK recorded rundll32.exe with a creation time of 2025-12-02, while Windows and System32 show 2024-04-01 creation, giving a bracketed window for when the LNK was staged on the threat actor's machine.  - The TrackerDataBlock names the build host "server" and records MAC address 00:50:56:c0:00:08 (a VMware NIC prefix), placing LNK creation inside a VM. The PropertyStoreDataBlock adds a user SID (S-1-5-21-2202213833-2675363039-2741304641-1002) and a parsing path under C:\Users\Public\Pictures, narrowing the actor's environment further.  - All metadata fields are fully populated, meaning the actor used no sanitization tool. Comparing these values across multiple LNK files from the same campaign allows clustering, as JPCERT/CC and APT29 researchers demonstrated: identical machine IDs, MACs, or volume serials link files even when hashes differ.  Parse every LNK with LECmd or a purpose-built tool and record all data blocks, not just the command line.  #DFIR_Radar
